title: fix(lint,metadata-protocol): the dataset publish door judges the dataset (#19143)
body:
Fixes #19143

Clause-②: yes

A runtime-created `dataset` reached ZERO author-time rules. It now dispatches the rules that were already written for it.

## First leg — re-taken independently on fetched `origin/main` (tip `7d0f911da9`, 2026-09-20)

All three of the card's legs reproduce. They are readings, not recollections.

**Leg 1 — the type is runtime-writable.** `packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-plugin.zod.ts:854`:

```
{ type: 'dataset', label: 'Dataset', … allowRuntimeCreate: true, supportsVersioning: true, executionPinned: false, loadOrder: 55, domain: 'ui' }
```

**Leg 2a — no rule declares it.** `git grep -n -A3 "runtimeTypes:" origin/main -- packages/lint/src` filtered for `dataset` returns **zero**. ⭐ LIT CONTROL, same grep, same corpus: the same window returns 14 `flow` hits across `authoring-rules.ts` and `reference-integrity-suite.ts` (the PM read 13 two hours earlier; `main` moved, the instrument did not). The zero is a reading, not a miss. Paths rather than counts: every `runtimeTypes:` declaration in the corpus sits in `packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts` and `packages/lint/src/reference-integrity-suite.ts`, and none of them names `dataset`.

**Leg 2b — no stack-key mapping.** `TYPE_TO_STACK_KEY` in `packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts`, read in full, held exactly `flow, object, view, action, page, dashboard, agent, hook, seed, permission, book`. No `dataset` row.

⭐ The two absences are **consistent, not contradictory** — the gate filters by `runtimeTypes` before it consults the table (`runtime-gate.ts`'s own `#8309` note). Neither is a broken wire, CI was green and correctly so, and what they sum to is that a dataset write built no per-write snapshot and dispatched no rule at all.

## The fork — arm (A), and the measurement that decided it

ADR-0049's 「声明即强制」 admits two resolutions. The decisive question is whether author-time rules for `dataset` exist at all. **They do**, named with file and symbol:

| rule | file | symbol | what it judges |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| the existence rules | `packages/lint/src/validate-dataset-references.ts` | `validateDatasetReferences` | `include[]`, `dimensions[].field`, `measures[].field`, filter KEYS |
| the aggregate rule | `packages/lint/src/validate-dataset-measure-aggregates.ts` | `validateDatasetMeasureAggregates` | `datasets[].measures[].aggregate` against the field's type |
| the base-object rung | `packages/lint/src/validate-object-references.ts` | `validateObjectReferences` | `datasets[].object` |

The failure mode the card names is a literal string in the first of them, `validate-dataset-references.ts:169`:

```
'that does not exist: the surface renders successfully with empty or wrong numbers, '
```

⇒ **arm (A): honour the declaration.** Two further readings confirm the same arm rather than leaving it a preference:

- `validateDatasetMeasureAggregates`' own registry entry carried a `surfaceReason` naming **this exact gap** as the only thing holding it off the door — "`TYPE_TO_STACK_KEY` in `runtime-gate.ts` has no `dataset` row … Mapping the `dataset` type at the gate is its own card";
- `RuntimeStackContext` already carried the `datasets` collection (#7529), and `metadata-protocol`'s `CLOSURE_CONTEXT_KEY_BY_TYPE` already carried `dataset: 'datasets'`. Every part of the host was in place. Retiring `allowRuntimeCreate` would have discarded working machinery to make a true statement false.

## ⚠️ The `seed: 'data'` hazard — a rule READS the key this maps onto

The wiring guard asks only that a declared type HAS a mapping, never that the mapping names a key some rule reads. Proof, not assertion:

- `validateDatasetReferences` opens with `recordsOf(stack.datasets)` (`validate-dataset-references.ts:182`);
- `validateDatasetMeasureAggregates` opens with `recordsOf(stack.datasets)` (`validate-dataset-measure-aggregates.ts:181`);
- `validateObjectReferences` walks `recordsOf(stack.datasets)` for the base-object rung (`validate-object-references.ts:401`).

And the proof that is not a grep: every one of them has a door control in `packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.dataset-writes.test.ts` that fires it through the real `runRuntimeAuthoringRules`, plus a case asserting the same snapshot goes clean when the defect is removed. A mapping wired onto nothing cannot produce those.

## What changed

- `TYPE_TO_STACK_KEY` gains `dataset: 'datasets'`, **in the same commit** as the declarations that read it — never a mapping ahead of its rules.
- `validateDatasetMeasureAggregates` crosses to `CLI_AND_RUNTIME` with `runtimeTypes: ['dataset']`; its stale `surfaceReason` is removed.
- The reference-integrity suite entry gains `dataset`; its per-member axis admits exactly `validateObjectReferences` and `validateDatasetReferences`, which cross together on #7220's reading (same document, split only by the severity ladder).
- `datasets` enters the derived name-keyed set by derivation with no second edit, so a finding leaving the gate reads `datasets.NAME.dimensions[0].field` rather than the gate's private snapshot index (#10064). Two pins in `runtime-gate.derived-name-keys.test.ts` reverse direction and are rewritten with the reason; the stale prose in `runtime-gate.derived-context-keys.test.ts` is corrected.
- No new rule and no new finding class. Rule ids and severities are unchanged.

⛔ **Not widened.** `validateWidgetBindings` and `validateChartBindings` read `stack.datasets` only as a resolution universe for a presentation; on a dataset write there is no board and no chart, so they keep their own doors. A DARK case pins that. No other metadata type's roster moved, and a DARK case pins that too.

## ⭐ False-positive measurement, before crossing

At the door's own shape — per-write snapshot, `RuntimeStackContext`, evaluated differentially exactly as `runtime-gate.ts` does — over **every dataset shipped in this monorepo**:

| source | datasets | own objects | rulesRun | findings |
|:---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `packages/platform-objects` · `system.datasets.ts` | 5 | (52 platform) | 2 | 0 |
| `examples/app-showcase` | 4 | 22 | 2 | 0 |
| `examples/app-crm` | 1 | 6 | 2 | 0 |
| `examples/app-todo` | 1 | 1 | 2 | 0 |
| **total** | **11** | | | **0** |

⭐ LIT CONTROL, same harness, same call: a synthetic probe with one dangling dimension path and one refused aggregate is **refused** with both ids and both name-keyed paths —

```
errors=["measure-aggregate-field-type-refused@datasets.probe_ds.measures[0].aggregate",
        "dataset-field-unknown@datasets.probe_ds.dimensions[0].field"]
```

So the zero is a fact about the corpus AND about the door: `rulesRun` read 2 on every shipped dataset, never 0.

## One fixture repaired, and why the expectation did not move

`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.adr0005-org-override-rollback.test.ts` went red on two cases. Its own docblock states the rule that decides the repair: *"spec validation runs before the authorization gate, so an invalid body would 422 first and this suite would pass without ever reaching the thing it pins."* The `dataset` probe body named `object: 'task'`, which resolves to nothing in that harness — it only ever reached the authorization gate because the door dispatched no rule for `dataset`. It now names `sys_user`, which resolves through `PLATFORM_PROVIDED_OBJECT_NAMES` with no object registry at all, so the body stays minimal and the 403 this file exists to pin stays measurable. ⛔ Changing the expectation to 422 would have deleted the test's subject.

A tree-wide sweep for the same shape found no other fixture affected: every test that writes a `dataset` through the publish door lives in `packages/metadata-protocol`, and that package's full suite is green.

## Verification — real exit codes, captured before any pipe

All readings taken in `../objectstack-issue-19143` at `990d41162c` unless noted.

| command | verdict |
|:---|:---|
| `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/lint^...' build` | **0** |
| `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/metadata-protocol^...' build` | **0** |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint test` | **0** — 106 files, 3993 tests passed (at `d0872564d6`; `packages/lint` untouched since) |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol test` | **0** — 181 files passed / 3 skipped, 2590 tests passed / 19 skipped |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol typecheck` | **0** |
| `pnpm lint` (repo-wide `eslint . --no-inline-config`, whole tree, no narrowing) | **0** |
| derived gate families (`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`) | 58 derived, 58 run, 0 UNRUN — **55 exit 0** |

Every heavy run went through `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` and its `VERDICT command-exit` line is the verdict quoted, never a bare `$?`.

**3 of the 58 are NOT MEASURED, not red.** Each exits **3** and says so in its own words — "PREREQUISITE NOT MET … ⛔ This is NOT a pass: nothing was measured":

- `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` — reads built output; 78 packages have no `dist/` in this worktree.
- `pnpm check:lean-entry-closure` — loads built entry points; `@objectstack/objectql/dist/core.mjs` absent.
- `pnpm check:type-check-debt` — refuses to re-measure with 24 workspace dependencies unbuilt, because a number recorded from there describes a different world.

All three want a whole-repo `pnpm build`, which this task built only two dependency closures of. CI checks out fresh and builds everything, so all three are answered there.

## Not in scope, recorded rather than fixed

- The publish door's refusal PRECEDENCE — the authoring gate fires ahead of `SysMetadataRepository.assertAllowed`, so a body that is both un-overridable and invalid answers 422 rather than 403. Surfaced by the fixture above; both are refusals, neither is silent, and this card changes no ordering.
- The suite docblock's "the runtime-publish axis" paragraph still lists the entry's types as "`flow` since #4463 P1, `view` since #9313"; it already omitted `object` (#15254) before this PR. Left as found.
